narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Minimalny dok" (OWNER's choice, variant C, APK 1356)**

The house is the screen. The model stands large and centred on a calm graphite ground, edge to edge, and the only chrome over it is a handful of small floating pieces of smoky matte glass: the house pill at the top start, "Dopasuj" and the menu at the top end, and a dock of two tiles at the foot — a wider "Cały dom" that names the layer shown now, and "Etapy". Each tile grows, as the very same piece of glass, into its own panel (Warstwy, Etapy) and shrinks back into its slot. Nothing else is permanent. Words are achromatic ink; one accent, mint, marks what is chosen or measured, always beside a mark or a word.

This direction replaces the former "Folding Rule" system and its bans (no pills, no shadows, a side rail, a bottom timeline panel). The folding rule survives as the construction axis inside the Etapy panel, now in mint; it is no longer the frame of the screen.

Confirmed rejections, from the owner's briefs: a permanent side rail, a permanent large progress panel, a full navigation bar (variant A), a vertical axis (variant B), a permanent CAD grid, card-heavy dashboards, stacked translucent panels, and dead features shown as main actions.
keyCharacteristics: The house fills most of the width upright and stays centred; the camera frames it in what the chrome leaves free AT REST.
Two dock tiles; each morphs into its panel. One panel at a time; the other tile stays where it is.
Smoky matte glass: tint, sheen, fixed grain, light rim, soft depth outside the shape. No backdrop blur (see Elevation & Depth).
One accent, mint, for chosen and measured things, never alone: a check, a filled mark, a heavier label go with it.
Rounded, soft shapes from one scale (12 / 18 / 22 / 26 dp and pills).
Every colour, space, corner, size, depth and motion comes from `Theme.kt` and `Motion.kt`.

rules.name: The Mint Means Chosen or Measured Rule
rules.body: The mint never marks an action, a focus or a link. A chosen thing is also a check, a filled mark or a heavier label.

rules.name: The Never Invented Rule
rules.body: With nothing saved, the Etapy tile says "Etapy" and nothing else: no percentage, no stage, no date.

rules.name: The Every maxLines Has An Ellipsis Rule
rules.body: Checked at font scale 1.3: the pill's name, the tile labels and the chips end in an ellipsis rather than wrap into the house.

rules.name: The One Layer Rule
rules.body: Glass is a one-layer material: two tints stacked never reach cover. A popup over glass (the ⋮ menu) takes `GlassOpaque`; dense lists live in opaque sheets.

rules.name: The Solid to the Finger Rule
rules.body: Every surface over the model takes `Modifier.solidToFinger()` first: it takes part in hit testing over its whole area without consuming anything, so a touch on glass never orbits the camera or picks a wall behind a label. The morphing glass is solid over exactly its current rectangle, and nothing outside it is; the 3D left uncovered stays live.

dos: take every colour, space, corner, size, depth and motion value from `Theme.kt` / `Motion.kt`.
keep the house the screen: frame it by the chrome at rest, centred, and never move the camera when a panel opens.
grow a panel out of the tile that opened it, as one surface, and close it back into the same slot.
say every state as a mark and a word (`stateDescription` on merged nodes), with mint only for chosen or measured things.
keep panel heads and the one way out outside the scroll, and fade a cut list or row.
check at font scale 1.3, with animations off, upright and on the side, and with the 3D uncovered still turning under a finger.
keep every touch target at least 48 dp, and every `maxLines` with an ellipsis.
donts: bring back the side rail, the permanent timeline panel, a navigation bar or a vertical axis.
stack translucent glass, or let a panel cover almost the whole screen on its side.
claim a backdrop blur, sample the 3D surface or read it back from the GPU.
run an animation loop at rest, or redraw the 3D when nothing changed — and don't fake it with a static picture.
show an invented percentage, stage or date when nothing is saved; a preview never saves.
expose a dead or unfinished feature as a main action; keep the full tools one tap away in the menu.
let the UI own semantic truth: layers come from the filter, views from the presets, stages from the session.
